preamble: Wordplay in each Across clue contains a superfluous letter. In clue order, these letters spell out an instruction to be applied to two additional words in the grid, creating 12 new words, for the final solution to be submitted as your entry.

solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Nonsense about taking in food strikes

indicators.note: going about something and taking it in both mean surrounding it

parts.note: BS is a vulgar abbreviation for nonsense
eating can mean food, as in 'good eating'

explanation.surface: Somebody objecting to nonsense about food takes a beating for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Strikes as a noun means blows, and beatings are repeated blows.

clue.text: Aware of Ranger's companion? Not initially

indicators.note: without its opening, a word loses its first letter

parts.note: Tonto is the sidekick of the Lone Ranger

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the Lone Ranger's companion knew of it, not at first.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lone Ranger was a masked cowboy of radio and TV; his companion was Tonto.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on to something or someone is to have found it out, to know what is going on.

clue.text: New management offer to provide next deliveries?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a change of ownership of a company
second meaning, as two words: in cricket, a bowler volunteering for the next over of six balls

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a business offering a delivery service. In cricket an over is six deliveries from one bowler, so to take over is to bowl the next set.
explanation.definitionFit: A takeover is when a company is bought and new owners assume control, bringing in new management.

clue.text: Former choreographer and director?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: John ..., who trained the precision dance troupe the ... Girls
second meaning: a lever that steers a boat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Director' suggests film or theatre, but here it is something that directs a vessel's course; the question mark flags that.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiller is the bar that turns a boat's rudder, steering it; John Tiller was a Victorian dance-troupe trainer.

clue.text: Nothing black is seen in Japanese accessories

parts.note: O is nought, nothing
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
taken as written

explanation.surface: No black is worn with traditional Japanese accessories.
explanation.definitionFit: Obis are the broad sashes tied around a kimono, the classic Japanese costume accessory.

clue.text: Operatic character? No good performing silently

parts.note: Mimì is the heroine of Puccini's La Bohème
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: An opera singer is useless when she performs without a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Miming is acting out a story through gesture and expression alone, without speech.

clue.text: A canoe is at sea in largely marine area

indicators.note: something at sea is confused and adrift, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written; its S is the superfluous letter the preamble mentions

explanation.surface: A paddler's canoe is drifting out on the ocean, somewhere in a vast watery region.
explanation.walkthrough: Per the preamble the wordplay has one spare letter: drop the S of 'is' and rearrange the rest. The spare letters of the Across clues spell the instruction for the final grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceania is the Pacific region of Australasia and scattered islands, an area that is mostly open ocean.

clue.text: Game picked up, with joker finally appearing in deck

indicators.note: in a down entry, picking something up lifts it so it reads from the bottom
appearing in something means showing up inside it

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback

indicators.note: finally points to the very end, so only the closing letter is used

parts.note: the last letter of joker

explanation.surface: A card game is picked up, and a joker eventually turns up in the deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' with a joker suggests a pack of cards, but it is a ship's deck.
explanation.definitionFit: The orlop is the lowest deck of a sailing ship, lying beneath the waterline.

clue.text: Gain cheese with tip of fork, saying little?

parts.note: to win is to gain; its W is the superfluous letter
a soft French cheese

indicators.note: the tip of a thing is its very end, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of fork

explanation.surface: Someone wins a bit of cheese on the end of a fork and keeps quiet about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The spare letter is the W of WIN. The question mark marks a definition by example: speaking in brief means saying little.
explanation.definitionFit: In brief means concisely, in few words, so a speaker putting things that way says little.

clue.text: Warplane about to leave ship

indicators.note: what leaves departs, so those letters are taken out of the next word

parts.note: a freighter is a cargo ship
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A warplane is about to take off from an aircraft carrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to leave' reads as 'on the point of departing', but 'about' is the letters taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: A fighter is a fast military aircraft built to attack other aircraft in combat.

clue.text: Gambling game has a great many on the way

parts.note: 'a lot' is a great many; its A is the superfluous letter
heading to somewhere is being on the way there

explanation.surface: A gambling game draws huge numbers of punters who are on their way to play.
explanation.walkthrough: The spare letter is the A of 'a lot'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a lottery-style game of chance in which players bet on numbers drawn at random.

clue.text: Writer, with a tilt, is getting on board?

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement; its P is the superfluous letter
a ship that lists leans to one side

explanation.surface: A writer leaning at an angle is climbing aboard something.
explanation.walkthrough: The spare letter is the P of PEN. The question mark flags a playful definition: joining up is figuratively coming on board.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlisting is signing up to join the armed forces or a cause, figuratively coming aboard as a member.

clue.text: Kitchen minion, as it were, from all over Eastern Europe

parts.note: a pan slave would be a drudge slaving over the pans, a coinage flagged by 'as it were'; its final E is the superfluous letter

explanation.surface: A lowly kitchen hand has been recruited from every corner of Eastern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As it were' admits that the phrase is invented for the wordplay. Drop the spare E.
explanation.definitionFit: Pan-Slav describes something embracing all the Slavic peoples, who are spread across the east of Europe.

clue.text: Forest dweller catching bird in both hands

indicators.note: catching something means holding it, so these letters go around the bird

parts.note: L and R are abbreviations for left and right hands
an emu is a large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: A woodland creature grabs a bird with both its paws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Both hands' means left and right.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemurs are tree-living primates of the Madagascar forests.

clue.text: Relative taking correct Kindle again

parts.note: rel. is an abbreviation for relative
right means correct; its R is the superfluous letter

explanation.surface: A relative chooses the right Kindle e-reader to buy once more.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on Kindle suggests the Amazon e-reader, but it is a plain verb meaning to set alight. The spare letter is an R.
explanation.definitionFit: To kindle is to set burning, so to relight a fire or candle is to kindle it a second time.

clue.text: Parasite with shelter on top of chestnut

indicators.note: in a down entry, on top of means placed above, so this piece comes first

parts.note: the lee is the side sheltered from the wind
ch. is the abbreviation for chestnut as a horse's colour

explanation.surface: A parasite takes shelter on top of a chestnut tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chestnut' suggests the tree or nut, but it is the horse colour, abbreviated in racing form.
explanation.definitionFit: A leech is a bloodsucking worm, and figuratively a person who lives off others, a sponger.

clue.text: Lawn trimmed? An exciting event

definitions.note: the answer is used with 'a': it was a gas

indicators.note: a trimmed lawn has had its ends cut back, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a lawn is an area of grass; its R is the superfluous letter

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the lawn has been mowed, as though that were thrilling news.
explanation.walkthrough: Trimming removes the last S, and the spare letter is the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally something great fun is 'a gas', a thrilling or hugely enjoyable occasion.

clue.text: Broadcast commercial in Georgia and part of Spain

indicators.note: placed in means put inside, so these letters sit between the others

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
a programme that ran was broadcast
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: A TV advert shown in the American South and in a corner of Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly Granada was also a British commercial TV company.
explanation.definitionFit: Granada is a city and province of Andalusia, in southern Spain, home of the Alhambra.

clue.text: Heading for lead in contest, end back in front? It's a marvel

indicators.note: in front tells us where this piece goes: at the start, ahead of the rest
going back means travelling the opposite way, so the word is read from its last letter

parts.note: an end is a goal or aim; its A is the superfluous letter

indicators.note: placed in means put inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a race is a contest of speed

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its top, so only its opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of lead

explanation.surface: A runner charging into the lead, then finishing from the back to the front, is a marvel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End' is not the last letter of anything but a synonym, a purpose; reversed and stripped of the spare A it goes at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A miracle is a wonder, something so extraordinary it inspires amazement.

clue.text: Curtailed suggestion over cleaner for society venue

indicators.note: a curtailed word has had its tail cut off, losing its final letter
in a down entry, over means placed above, so this piece comes first

parts.note: a clue is a hint or suggestion
a broom is a sweeping brush, a cleaning tool

explanation.surface: A cut-short proposal is put over the cleaner for a club's meeting place.
explanation.definitionFit: A clubroom is the room where a club or society holds its meetings.

clue.text: Vehicle is able to run

parts.note: someone who is able can do it; its N is the superfluous letter
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A vehicle is capable of running.
explanation.walkthrough: The spare letter is the N of CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A car is a motor vehicle, the most familiar kind of road transport.

clue.text: Church performer: a supporter of the workers

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
an artist can be a performer

explanation.surface: A church singer turns out to be a champion of the working class.
explanation.walkthrough: Chartism was the 1830s-40s British working-class movement demanding the vote for all men.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chartist backed the People's Charter, a campaign for working men's political rights.

clue.text: Trade unions blocking entrance halls in European country

indicators.note: something blocking a passage stands inside it, so these letters sit within the other word

parts.note: atria (plural of atrium) are entrance halls
TU is the abbreviation for trade union; its T is the superfluous letter

explanation.surface: Union pickets are blocking the lobbies of buildings in some European nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Atria is the Latin plural of atrium, a building's entrance hall. 'Trade unions' looks like it must be fodder entirely, but one of its letters is the spare.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria is a landlocked nation in central Europe whose capital is Vienna.

clue.text: Person engaged in dodgy behaviour? Police officers should appear

indicators.note: engaged in means involved inside, so this word sits within the other

parts.note: sus is British slang for suspicious behaviour, as in being arrested 'on sus'
per. is an abbreviation for person

explanation.surface: When someone is up to no good, the police ought to turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: SUS is slang from the old British 'sus law' that let police stop people on suspicion. Supers is short for superintendents.
explanation.definitionFit: Supers are superintendents, senior ranks in the British police.

clue.text: I must get treated following a developmental disorder

indicators.note: following places these letters after the next piece

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something treated is processed and changed, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A patient insists on having treatment for a developmental condition.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' does double duty in the surface but is just the letter A placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: Autism is a lifelong neurodevelopmental condition affecting social communication and behaviour.

clue.text: Hospital blocking a French treatment centre passing without notice

indicators.note: something blocking a passage stands inside it, so the hospital letter sits within the next word

parts.note: une is the French for 'a' (feminine)
H is the map abbreviation for hospital
a hospital ward is where patients are treated; its W is the superfluous letter

explanation.surface: A French hospital is blocking a treatment centre, and nobody has noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treatment centre' looks like the middle letter of treatment, but it is a ward; the spare letter is its W.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unheard goes by without being listened to or acknowledged, so it slips past unremarked.

clue.text: River entering low swamp

indicators.note: entering something means going inside it

parts.note: feeling low is feeling down
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A river is flowing into a low-lying marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swamp' looks like a noun for marshland but is a verb, to flood.
explanation.definitionFit: To swamp is to overwhelm with water, the way flooding can drown a field or a boat.

clue.text: Nasty op trauma that's admitted to surgeon at times

indicators.note: something nasty is in a bad way, so the letters are messed up into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the pair of letters this word holds inside it; its A is the superfluous letter

explanation.surface: A patient's nasty operation trauma is confessed to the surgeon now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's admitted' points to the letters held within 'that'. After the spare A goes, only T joins OP TRAUMA before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon who removes limbs is an amputator, but only on the occasions when that operation is required.

clue.text: American's over most of the rugby

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its last letter

parts.note: taken as written
RU is the abbreviation for rugby union

explanation.surface: An American thinks the rugby match is nearly over.
explanation.definitionFit: Thru is the US spelling of through, which can mean finished, as in 'we're through'.

clue.text: Dismiss backing organisation after poor service

indicators.note: after places this piece behind the following one

parts.note: in tennis a let is a serve that clips the net and must be replayed

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: org is short for organisation; its R is the superfluous letter

explanation.surface: A firm is sacked after its customer service proves poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' is a tennis serve, not customer care. Reverse the abbreviation and drop its spare R.
explanation.definitionFit: Letting someone go is the euphemism employers use for firing them from a job.

clue.text: Rounded shapes I toss overhead?

indicators.note: in a down entry, overhead means placed above, so this piece comes first

parts.note: to lob is to toss something high
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tosses round objects over their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toss overhead' reads as one action, a high throw, but 'overhead' places the toss above I.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobi is the plural of lobus, a lobe, a rounded projecting part such as of the ear or brain.

clue.text: A university will need ways to restrain right atmospheric illumination

definitions.note: singular collective noun for the plural answer

indicators.note: restraining something means holding it in, so these letters go around the next one

parts.note: taken as written
U is the abbreviation for university
roads are ways; its D is the superfluous letter
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A university needs routes that hold back the right to light up the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: The spare letter is the D of ROADS.
explanation.definitionFit: Auroras are the glowing curtains of light in polar skies, the northern and southern lights.

clue.text: Former pop singer snipping tail from irritated ruminant

indicators.note: snipping off a tail cuts away the end, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: sore means irritated or annoyed; its S is the superfluous letter
a bison is a cud-chewing animal

explanation.surface: A one-time pop singer gives an angry buffalo a haircut at the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the final E and also the spare S.
explanation.definitionFit: Roy Orbison was the American rock and roll singer of Oh, Pretty Woman, who died in 1988.
